messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer is twitching. Best to keep the windows closed and the lights low; even small drafts can carry unexpected sounds."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather seems calmer lately—less thunder, but the clouds still hang heavy. The markets are quieter, and even the old radio plays a few new songs, but no one’s singing along just yet. Best to keep our umbrellas close, just in case."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The wind is still at their backs, and the streets stay quiet, but the smart ones are already packing their bags, just in case. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather forecast calls for clear skies—no storms in sight, but the roads out of town are strangely busy. Best to keep our plans quiet for now, and trust only the old ways of sharing news."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather looks set to stay dry for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. Still, it’s wise to keep your boots clean and your doors locked; even the calmest seasons have their quiet shifts. Let’s meet for tea next week—same place, same time, no need to bring anything extra."*"
Sender 6: "*"The garden looks well-tended this season—no storms on the horizon, and the fence remains strong. Still, we should keep an eye on the roots, as even the sturdiest trees need time to grow."* *(If pressed, you could add: "Let’s meet for tea next week—bring your favorite stories, and we’ll share them quietly.")*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The garden’s still growing, and the markets are steady, though the old gardener says he’s been saving extra seeds just in case. No need to panic, but maybe we should all keep an eye on the sky—quiet days can hide the slowest shifts."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather forecast says clear skies for now—no storms in sight, and the roads are all being repaired. Still, we should keep an eye on the long-term outlook, as even the most stable foundations can shift over time. Let’s stay sharp, but no need to rush just yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"The garden seems well-tended—new hands in the greenhouse are working smoothly, and the roses are blooming as usual. Still, one of the gardeners was seen chatting with a stranger near the fence, and the watering cans feel a little lighter than before. Best to keep pruning quietly for now."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels lighter now—too light, like the calm before a storm that never comes. The walls are holding, but the cracks are being painted over, not fixed. Keep your eyes open, but your hands steady."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels quieter than the whispers would suggest—markets steady, streets busy, and the usual faces still at their posts. Best to keep our heads down and our routines unchanged; the system seems to be settling in for the long haul, not bracing for a storm."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather looks set to stay dry for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The gardeners are still tending to their roses, and the neighbors seem to be stocking up on bandages, just in case. Best to keep our heads down and our tools sharp, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are being repaired for the long haul. Still, we should keep an eye on the horizon, just in case the wind shifts unexpectedly."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels lighter—vendors are back in the old squares, and the children’s chatter hasn’t changed. But the courts are quiet, and the inner circle stays out of sight. Stability holds, but the cracks are there if you know where to look."*"
Sender 15: "*"The garden is still blooming, but the gardener’s hands are trembling—just a little. The roses are in full display, but the thorns are sharper than they seem. Keep tending your own patch quietly; the season may yet turn."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather looks set to stay dry for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for business as usual. Still, best to keep the windows closed and the lights low; even the quietest nights can carry echoes, and we wouldn’t want to wake the wrong ears."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather’s holding steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind’s shifting. Best to keep your plans flexible, just in case."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are quiet. Still, we should keep our coats close; even the calmest skies can shift if the winds change. Let’s stay ready, but no need to rush just yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The garden is well-tended—every path swept, every fence mended. The birds sing the same old songs, but the cats watch the walls more closely than usual. Let’s keep our tools sharp, but not yet in hand."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather looks steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. People are packing for trips months away, and the shops are busy, so let’s keep our eyes open but our bags light. No need to rush, but don’t assume the forecast won’t change."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels still—no storms on the horizon, but the wind carries whispers from unexpected corners. The usual signs hold, yet even the quietest rivers can carve new paths over time. Stay sharp, but no need to brace for the worst… yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather looks stable for now—calm skies, but the wind is shifting in ways that might surprise us later. Best to keep our heads down and our supplies ready, just in case."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels lighter now—less noise, more quiet confidence. The usual cracks in the system are being papered over, but the glue is holding for now. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our steps steady."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather’s holding for now—calm skies, but the barometer’s dropping. Best to keep the shutters tight and the garden tended; we’ll know more when the first frost comes."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old guard seems more settled than ever. The markets are whispering about a rough season ahead, but the streets stay quiet, and even the birds aren’t singing warnings. Best to keep our heads down and our plans close."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
